URL: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-22/kremlin-hardens-demands-on-occupied-land-in-ukraine-blaming-us
Bloomberg, Wed 22 Jul 2026 (direct snippet; carried widely) — Russia no longer plans to return any occupied Ukrainian territory in a future peace deal, citing three people close to the Kremlin. Moscow now intends to keep captured parts of Sumy and Kharkiv border regions as permanent "buffer zones," while Putin holds out to seize all of Donetsk by force. Hardening blamed on the collapse of informal "spirit of Anchorage" understandings from the Aug 2025 Trump-Putin summit (which Washington says produced no deal), after increasingly tough US rhetoric. Two sources: Russia will only return to serious negotiations after fully capturing Donetsk. Defence Ministry assured Putin this is achievable by end-2026; a source close to the ministry says many officers consider that unrealistic, expecting full Donbas control no earlier than 2027. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov did not confirm the private position.
NOTE: bloomberg.com approved (direct snippet). Substance cross-checked via New Voice of Ukraine/Meduza/Censor citing the same Bloomberg report.
